taxonomic_note: Accepted species and Texas-native at the state level, but it fails the project's current target-zone native rule.
look_here_first: Look at the leaf immediately: American holly is the big-leaved evergreen tree, with thick dark-green leaves bearing prominent stiff spine-tipped teeth.

project_inclusion.range_basis: USDA-derived Texas county-native data document American holly in eastern/southeastern Texas but no current project target-zone counties.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Texas-native at state level does not satisfy the project's >=3 target-county rule. Planted or escaped Central Texas trees do not change native classification.

best_field_traits: evergreen tree, often pyramidal when young
leaves substantially larger than yaupon leaves
margins commonly armed with stiff spine-tipped teeth
upper surface dark glossy green; lower surface paler
female trees produce persistent bright-red drupes
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use this as the large-spiny-leaf nursery/landscape holly comparison; it must remain excluded from project-native totals.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Yaupon has tiny evergreen leaves with low rounded teeth. Possumhaw is deciduous with thinner non-spiny leaves. Chinese holly is a common introduced ornamental with strongly horned leaves and should be separated using leaf shape and horticultural context.
